To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the internationalisation of small firms can be described as a process of gradual, evolutionary change, but also as a process of rapid, revolutionary change.

“The internationalisation process of small and medium sized enterprises is influenced by their internationalisation pathway, and the pathway can be determined by the firm’s internationalisation history, the firm’s resources, and the firm’s environment.

(1) there are three main pathways of small firm internationalisation, which can be labelled ‘born global’, ‘born-again global’ and ‘incremental’; (2) the three pathways differ significantly in terms of their strategic orientation and the way in which the firms manage the internationalisation process; (3) the three pathways also differ significantly in terms the firms' internationalisation performance, in that ‘born globals’ and ‘born-again globals’ outperform ‘incremental’ firms
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: ‘How do firms internationalise?’
the question of how firms internationalise and what determines their internationalisation behaviour.
the internationalisation of the firm and its impact on the development of the international business environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the internationalisation process of small firms is a complex phenomenon, and the literature has been unable to develop a comprehensive and integrated theory.
the internationalisation behaviour of firms is a function of the firm's size and age and the internationalisation pathway that it has followed.
the internationalisation process of small firms is a dynamic and complex process, which is influenced by a variety of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the internationalisation process is more complex and diverse than previously thought and that it is not possible to develop a ‘one-size-fits-all’ model.
the ‘born global’ firms and the ‘born-again global’ firms are not only different from the traditional incremental internationalising firms, but also different from each other.
there is a need to move beyond the traditional linear models of internationalisation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
internationalisation pathways should be recognised as an important dimension in the internationalisation process.
the traditional ‘stage’ model of firm internationalisation needs to be updated to recognise the existence of different pathways to internationalisation.
there is no ‘one size fits all’ model of internationalisation.
